scope: Current, review-worthy Part 2 claims only. Historical model rows, exploratory diagnostics and superseded results remain in prose but are not governed claims.
tolerance_semantics: absolute_tolerance is used only to match the registry value to the authority's expected literal. The authoritative notebook's own check() tolerance governs live-data acceptance and may be wider.

claims.statement: The evaluated candidate population is the deduplicated union of the GGD, GPGD and GCD routes: 6,685,686 pairs at a 1.89% positive rate.
claims.interpretation: This is the population on which current validation claims are defined; it is not every disease crossed with every gene.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb2, then review pool/split denominators and every listed consumer whenever a route, seed gate or graph input changes.

claims.statement: The adopted champion is m7-f14-cal, saved model W8VhjZOZ, with 14 features: m7-f14 with sigmoid-calibrated output (retrained 2026-11-10 on the R5 graph).
claims.interpretation: Model identity is governed by the repository model registry; model quality is governed separately and cannot be inferred from identity alone.
claims.review_policy: A champion change requires model-registry review plus all governed validation checks; never retarget consumers from a metric alone.

claims.statement: Champion reconstruction fidelity is macro per-disease AUROC 0.8180 across 604 held-out diseases.
claims.interpretation: This measures within-disease recovery of known associations; it is not therapeutic efficacy, causal validity or prospective success.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb3 and review the distribution and denominator before changing any headline; report the macro value with its 604-disease scope.

claims.statement: Pooled AUROC is 0.8908, about seven points above macro per-disease AUROC 0.8180, because pooling lets large diseases dominate.
claims.interpretation: The macro value is the governed headline. The pooled value exists only as a warning and must not be substituted for it.
claims.review_policy: Fail review if pooled and macro semantics are collapsed, if the pooled value is promoted to the headline, or if either value changes without nb3 evidence.

claims.statement: Family-level validation covers 478 families with macro AUROC 0.8003.
claims.interpretation: Family grouping is a leakage-control view, not evidence that every family or disease performs uniformly.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb3 after split-family or champion changes and retain the warning that the aggregate hides family-level variation.

claims.statement: Association ranking and therapeutic agreement are essentially uncorrelated: drug-target macro AUROC is 0.6703, Pearson r is +0.167 and R-squared is 0.0278 across 122 evaluable diseases (t = +1.85, not significant at 0.05).
claims.interpretation: Association AUROC cannot be used as a proxy for therapeutic relevance; every result must name its axis.
claims.review_policy: Review association and therapeutic axes together after model or drug-label changes; never describe association AUROC as therapeutic prediction.

claims.statement: Among known targets, rho(degree, probability) is 0.3472 and the share the model calls positive rises from 10.2% in the lowest degree quintile to 52.1% in the highest; mean calibrated probability rises from 0.0915 to 0.2257 (spread 0.1341).
claims.interpretation: Hub bias is a current measured weakness, and it grew with the 2026-11-07 retrain (rho 0.3273 to 0.3500; detection swing 3.3x to 4.4x) and held at that level after the 2026-11-10 retrain on the R5 graph (rho 0.3472; detection swing 5.1x). Since 2026-11-07 probabilities are sigmoid-calibrated, so the mean-probability values and the spread are on a different scale from earlier raw-score values and must not be compared with them; compare rho and the detection swing. The older claim that the champion improved under-studied targets was refuted.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb3b after champion, feature-population or split changes; preserve the negative finding and do not infer a cause without a controlled test.

claims.statement: Drug-target AUROC is 0.6703 over all positives and 0.7362 over route-supported positives.
claims.interpretation: The gap is evidence about scoreability and outcome-selected route support, not permission to discard hard positives or optimise the candidate gate on drug labels.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb2 when route eligibility or the drug benchmark changes; report both estimands and the outcome-selection warning.

claims.statement: Among novel top-ranked candidates, approved drug targets are enriched 22.94-fold at K=10 and 4.98-fold at K=200.
claims.interpretation: This supports discovery enrichment inside the admitted pool, but a drug-target lookup can reward gene popularity and must remain a warning-bearing secondary benchmark.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb4/nb6 after champion, ranking-population or drug-ground-truth changes; retain both the pool scope and gene-popularity warning.

claims.statement: Degree-matched tractability lift is 3.06-fold pooled and 2.85-fold macro at K=10, and 2.30-fold pooled at K=200; pooled exceeds the naive lift from K=20 on and falls just below it at K=10; macro exceeds it at every K (since the 2026-11-10 retrain).
claims.interpretation: Pooled and macro are different estimands and both are reported; the deeper-list pooled value is the more stable model-selection corroboration.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb4/nb6 after model or candidate-population changes; never merge pooled and macro lifts or compare them without naming K.

claims.statement: HER2-positive breast carcinoma reconstructs at AUROC 0.9385, while HER2-positive and triple-negative disease share only 2 novel top-50 candidates; triple-negative has only 8 known targets.
claims.interpretation: The molecular-subtype separation is useful, but the thin triple-negative label makes its own AUROC unquotable and the panel remains a clinician falsification exercise.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb4 and nb7 after graph, champion or panel changes; do not quote thin-disease AUROC and keep clinician-review defects visible.

claims.statement: The candidate pool covers 98.5% of curated drug-target pairs across evaluable diseases; pool size has Spearman correlation +0.081 with coverage and only 2 diseases fall below 50% coverage.
claims.interpretation: Reachability is a real per-disease limitation but not a broad sparse-disease failure; pathless pairs still need a feature family that can score them.
claims.review_policy: Re-run nb2 after graph-route or seed-gate changes; preserve both the high aggregate coverage and the pathless-pair limitation.
